issues.description: Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal, so transient states can block later legitimate lifecycle updates.
Same-rank records do not compare timestamps, allowing older RUNNING or terminal rows to overwrite newer job data.
Report and top commands call the same create-if-missing DB path as ingest, so a typo silently creates an empty database.
Database connection always initializes schema and parent directories, with no read-only/open-existing mode for reporting workflows.
Parser accepts negative CPU/GPU allocations and empty user or partition fields, which can produce nonsensical reports.
Failure classification is hard-coded narrowly and misses common Slurm failure-like states such as NODE_FAIL, BOOT_FAIL, PREEMPTED, and DEADLINE.
Usage reports filter with COALESCE over text timestamps, preventing efficient indexed range scans as the jobs table grows.
Schema has no indexes for reference-time or report grouping queries, so all reporting paths will trend toward full table scans.
Timezone-aware timestamps are preserved as text instead of normalized, so lexicographic comparisons can disagree with chronological order.
